reason: Reproduced exactly, at all seven widths. Recipe: owner-flight, open Edit on 'invitations' (23 days, 2026-08-08), press -7 once. It lands on 2026-08-01, the same day as 'menu' (16 days), and the pair becomes data-stack lead/follow. Escape closes the editor. Then a real pointer click at the centre of the LEAD row's own .b-grab: at 390x844, 768x1024, 1024x800, 1152x800, 1279x800, 1280x900 and 1440x960 the click event target is DIV.b-item[data-id=demo-audience-item-invitations] - the FOLLOW row - and nothing at all happens. Not the wrong editor: after the click, no .b-item[data-editing=true] exists, no .b-grab has aria-expanded=true, document.activeElement is unchanged, no page error. elementsFromPoint at the lead grab's centre returns ['DIV.b-item@invitations','BUTTON.b-grab','SPAN.b-grabWord'] - the follow row's box is topmost, the lead's own button is second. The mechanism is as stated and is in the source: b.css:175 .b-item{position:absolute} pins the row to its true pixel, b.css:249 .b-copy{margin-top:var(--push)} pushes only the words, and .b-item is an absolutely-positioned BFC so the margin lives inside it - the row's box therefore starts on the true pixel and runs push+copy tall, with a transparent band on top. Measured --push on the follow row is 93px at 390 and 102px at 768 and every width above, and that band lies over the lead row's copy. render-b.js:984 delegates on event.target.closest('.b-grab') then closest('[data-act]'); a click landing on the bare .b-item matches neither, so it is silently discarded. The gates are blind to it exactly as claimed: interaction-check.mjs:2306-2311 asserts the pair forms, shares one mark and one count, is grouped not overprinted, sits on the true pixel and is announced - never that either row stays pressable; and the two crowding audits at :2412 and :2451 explicitly 'continue' past data-stack=follow rows. Only b.css:235 (the decorative leader) sets pointer-events anywhere in the CSS, and there is no pointerdown/mousedown handler in render-b.js, so nothing depends on the row box taking a pointer. I injected the proposed rule at runtime with the stack formed: elementsFromPoint at the lead grab's centre becomes ['BUTTON.b-grab','SPAN.b-grabWord',...], the click opens the LEAD row's editor (data-editing=menu, aria-expanded=true on menu's grab, focus moves to #b-edit), and the hover affordance survives - .b-item:hover still matches when the pointer is over .b-title, the grab still resolves to opacity 1 and the crowded .b-copy still paints its hover fill. The row it takes out is the nearest one, the only one wearing the indigo lead mark, and on a phone there is no tab key to route around it. Keyboard-only survival is not a mitigation on the flagship case, where a wedding day holds ceremony, photographs, dinner and first dance on one date.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as proposed, in b.css beside the .b-copy rule that carries --push: .b-item { pointer-events: none; } and .b-item .b-copy, .b-item .b-away, .b-item .b-tick { pointer-events: auto; }. Verified: nothing else inside .b-item needs a pointer (the only other child is the visually-hidden .b-unitSaid), no JS listens on the row box, and both decorative pseudo-elements are already inert or become so harmlessly. Do NOT scope it to [data-crowded=true] - push is written by script after layout, and an unscoped rule cannot fall out of step with it. Two sharpenings to the gate assertion: (1) assert it with the editor CLOSED as well as open, because the collision window is transient and the docked sheet can cover the pair while it is open; (2) run it at 390 as well as 1440 - the band is 93px at phone width and 102px above 768, so a desk-only assertion would miss a phone-only regression. Assertion: after the stack forms, for every .b-grab in .b-measure, document.elementFromPoint at its centre must resolve inside its own .b-item - and, stronger and cheap, click the lead row's grab and assert its aria-expanded flips to true.
